intake.goal: Draft an external email to Acme Cloud operations requesting manual checks and incident status updates for a sensitive EU customer notification pipeline runtime incident.
intake.context: Incident detected 09:12 CET on May 25, 2026; intermittent delivery failures for transactional notifications; still under investigation; no confirmed data loss; delayed processing observed for some EU tenants; likely impacts customer notification pipeline; need status back to incident lead within 60 minutes; prefer official EU sources.
intake.domain_label: Email drafting to operations team for EU runtime incident notification pipeline
success_criteria: Email is ready to send and clearly requests the specified queue/backlog verification steps.
Email includes all provided incident facts and the 60-minute reporting requirement.
Email asks explicitly whether impact extended beyond the notification pipeline.
Email uses appropriate, non-speculative language consistent with 'still under investigation' and 'no confirmed data loss'.
Recipient, subject/message intent, and action items are unambiguous.
constraints: Email is addressed to the operations team at Acme Cloud.
Include incident timing details (09:12 CET on May 25, 2026).
Mention symptoms (intermittent delivery failures for transactional notifications; delayed processing for some EU tenants; no confirmed data loss).
Ask operations to manually verify delivery queues.
Ask operations to check retry backlog.
Ask operations to confirm whether customer-facing impact extended beyond the notification pipeline.
Request a status report back to the incident lead within 60 minutes.
Prefer using official EU sources when referencing compliance/impact context.

planner_rationale: Draft a sensitive, action-oriented external email to Acme Cloud operations. The email must include incident timing, observed symptoms, explicitly request manual verification of delivery queues and retry backlog, ask whether customer-facing impact extended beyond the notification pipeline, and require a status update back to the incident lead within 60 minutes. Language should remain non-speculative and consistent with “still under investigation” and “no confirmed data loss,” with careful handling of EU-compliance context by referring to official EU sources where relevant.

plan_steps.objective: Establish the email’s purpose and audience-specific framing for a sensitive EU incident with operations.
plan_steps.rationale: Operations recipients need an unambiguous incident request with appropriate seriousness and confidentiality signaling, without over-claiming facts not yet confirmed.
plan_steps.expected_outcome: A clear opening intent that identifies the recipient group, states the message is for a sensitive incident, and sets the expectation of rapid operational checks and a time-bound update.

plan_steps.objective: Include core incident details exactly as provided (timing and affected behavior) using cautious, non-speculative phrasing.
plan_steps.rationale: The email must convey incident timing (09:12 CET on May 25, 2026), the observed symptoms (intermittent transactional delivery failures; delayed processing for some EU tenants), and the current certainty level (“still under investigation,” “no confirmed data loss”).
plan_steps.expected_outcome: A concise incident summary section that accurately reflects known facts and clearly labels what is suspected vs. confirmed.

plan_steps.objective: Request manual verification of delivery queues for the transactional notification pipeline and related EU-tenant processing.
plan_steps.rationale: The task explicitly requires asking operations to manually verify delivery queues to check whether notifications are being stuck, dropped, or otherwise failing to progress.
plan_steps.expected_outcome: An explicit action item instructing operations to manually inspect relevant delivery queues for signs of blockage, failure, or processing imbalance affecting EU tenants.

plan_steps.objective: Request checks of the retry backlog and retry/processing pipeline health to determine whether intermittent failures are accumulating.
plan_steps.rationale: Retry backlog status is directly tied to intermittent delivery failures and delayed processing; verifying it helps determine scope and whether backlog growth is driving user impact.
plan_steps.expected_outcome: A second explicit action item requiring operations to check retry backlog depth, growth rate, and whether retries are being successfully drained.

plan_steps.objective: Ask operations to confirm the scope of customer-facing impact beyond the notification pipeline.
plan_steps.rationale: The constraint requires an explicit question about whether impact extended beyond the notification pipeline, ensuring incident scoping is addressed early.
plan_steps.expected_outcome: A clearly worded question asking whether any other customer-facing systems or workflows were impacted, and if so, what boundaries are known as of the update time.

plan_steps.objective: Set a strict status-update requirement back to the incident lead within 60 minutes and specify what information to include.
plan_steps.rationale: The runtime context mandates a status back to the incident lead within 60 minutes; specifying the expected content reduces back-and-forth and speeds decisioning for the EU customer notification process.
plan_steps.expected_outcome: A time-boxed request stating that operations should return a status report within 60 minutes, including findings from queue verification, retry backlog checks, and any confirmed/observed customer impact scope.

plan_steps.objective: Add a sensitivity-appropriate confidentiality/handling note and ensure language consistency throughout the email.
plan_steps.rationale: High sensitivity requires avoiding unnecessary details while still being operationally useful; also, careful wording helps prevent misinterpretation in an incident context.
plan_steps.expected_outcome: A short confidentiality line (and any appropriate sensitivity labeling) plus consistent use of cautious terms (e.g., “still under investigation,” “no confirmed data loss”).

plan_steps.objective: Incorporate compliance/impact context using appropriate references to official EU sources where relevant, without making speculative claims.
plan_steps.rationale: The constraints prefer official EU sources when referencing compliance/impact context. This helps frame why manual verification is important while staying accurate and non-speculative.
plan_steps.expected_outcome: A brief, non-speculative compliance context statement that points to official EU regulatory guidance as relevant (without overcommitting to conclusions about legal impact).

plan_steps.objective: Finalize the email structure (subject and message) so recipient actions are unambiguous and scannable.
plan_steps.rationale: For incident emails, clear structure (incident summary, action requests, timing requirements) improves operational response speed.
plan_steps.expected_outcome: A ready-to-send email with an unambiguous subject line, a succinct incident narrative, clearly enumerated action items (queue verification, retry backlog check, impact scope confirmation), and the 60-minute status requirement.
